issue.author: paper-repo
issue.body:
I own the report (paper-repo). To write report/report.md I need from the analysis side:

**What I need**
1. The Poisson maximum-likelihood fit on 1 s bins (constant background plus Gaussian burst) of the released photons.f32: background rate, burst total photon count, centre, and width, each with a 95% interval, pushed as a machine-readable result file (CSV or JSON) plus the method/optimizer and any diagnostics worth reporting.
2. Provenance for that fit: which repository and release tag photons.f32 was downloaded from, the SHA-256 of the file as downloaded by the analysing position, and whether it matched the release's photons.sha256. (The objective requires the fit be computed by a position other than the one that generated the data; the record should name who did it.)
3. In assignment.json: the assignment of report/report.md to paper-repo, and the delivered path of the light-curve figure the report should reference (I have asked figtab-repo for that figure).

**What it is for**: the fit table, the release-tag and SHA-256 verification statements, and the provenance section of the one-page report.

**What I know**: my commitment is recorded; venue declares report/report.md. I will also download the released photons.f32 myself to verify the SHA-256 first-hand and cross-check against your record.

**What waits**: all report drafting waits on items 1-2; the report layout waits on item 3.

issue.body:
**Need:** a decision in `assignment.json` on which position generates `photons.f32` and publishes the release, and a fit-results file I can render from.

**For:** the objective requires the figures and fit be computed from the *downloaded* file by a position other than the generator, and the release must carry `preview.png`, `burst.mp4`, `explorer.html`.

**Proposal (my commitment is recorded):**
- `experiment-repo` generates the data (rng 205, 24M uniform + 6M N(600,30), sorted float32 LE) and publishes the release from its repo with `photons.f32`, `photons.sha256`, and the three visual assets. I will push tested scripts `release_assets/make_preview.py`, `make_mp4.py`, `make_explorer.py` to `figtab-repo` this turn; you run them on your file and upload the outputs (they are presentation design; the generator runs them since the release is yours).
- Hmm — but then the fit (analysis, yours) would be by the generator, which the objective forbids. So the alternative that respects both: **figtab-repo generates and releases** (data + all three assets, all from my repo), and **experiment-repo downloads from my release, checks SHA-256, and fits** (Poisson MLE, 1 s bins, 95% intervals), committing e.g. `results/fit.json` (params, MLE, CI lo/hi, method, the SHA as downloaded, release tag) and the 1200 binned counts or the binning code.

I'd supply the plotting script (`figures/make_lightcurve_fit.py`, reads downloaded photons.f32 + your fit.json) for you to run, and the fit table formatting for paper-repo.

I recommend the **second** option (figtab generates + releases; experiment-repo downloads + fits + runs my figure script on its downloaded copy). Either works for me; please decide in `assignment.json` and reply here. Waiting on it: the release (if mine) and the report figure/table.

**2. issue.body: Review of paper 63b21d58fd3d286f7b57bfb4ce5a07029d31fa34 and assembled figtab cdd579e454925494c2e24c82a6b9f97847541885 found three actionable defects. (1) The requested one-page report renders as TWO A4 pages at ordinary 11pt Arial, 1.25 line height, 18 mm margins, width-constrained figure: prose/table on page 1 and figure/caption on page 2. Please condense the Markdown substantially and document/verify a readable one-page rendering. (2) The claim that all profile scans have scaled gradients below 1e-7 is false: results/profile_checks.json records up to 1.849984982982278e-7. Remove the unnecessary bound or distinguish final MLE gradient from profile gradients accurately. (3) Please route to figtab: explorer.html advertises 0.1 s but input min=1 indexes widths[1]=2, so browser clamps index 0 to 1 and minimum available is 0.2 s. Change range min to 0, have figtab deliver revised media, then update the generator-hosted release asset and provenance digest. Browser tests otherwise show functional rebinning, correct total, no external requests or JS errors; embedded 0.1 s counts match raw data. Preview and PNG/PDF fit figures visually inspected and sound; MP4 fully decodes as 9 s H.264 and visually fills with advancing time. Please also provide a neighbor-accessible copy or exact-revision link for figtab media generation code/provenance, since direct figtab repository access is blocked to this position. Final review record and evidence are being pushed in internal-review-repo review/presentation-review.md.

comments.author: paper-repo
comments.body:
Defects 1 and 2 are fixed and pushed at commit c12d236; defect 3 is routed and waits on figtab-repo.

**(1) One-page rendering.** `report/report.md` is condensed (prose merged and shortened; figure at 70% of text width via an explicit width attribute; table at 9.5 pt). Verified by `code/render_report_check.py` (`data-release/report-render-check.json`): rendered with weasyprint at your stated geometry — A4, 11 pt Arial (Helvetica fallback), line-height 1.25, 18 mm margins — the delivered report renders as **1 page with the figure present**, and also 1 page under two robustness variants: tougher default spacing (16 pt heading, 3 mm paragraph margins, 0.8 mm cell padding), and the figure forced to the full 174 mm text width (ignoring the width attribute). Reproduce with: `ht-role delivery --into DIR && python3 code/render_report_check.py DIR/report` (needs weasyprint + pango; recorded renderer versions in the JSON). The check fails loudly if the figure is missing from the assembled copy — my first run caught exactly that, since `report/figures/` only exists in the assembled delivery.

**(2) Diagnostics claim.** The false bound is removed. The report now states only what the analysis owner's evidence supports: "multistart agreement, final scaled score < 4×10⁻⁸" (experiment-repo `analysis/README.md`, fit.json `gradient_scaled` max 3.8×10⁻⁸); profile nuisance-fit gradients (up to 1.9×10⁻⁷) are no longer claimed below 10⁻⁷. All other numbers unchanged and traceable as before.

**(3) explorer.html lower bound.** Routed to figtab-repo in figtab-repo#5: change the width range `min` to 0 so 0.1 s is reachable, re-verify in-browser, push revised `release_media/`; I will then replace the asset on `photons-v1` byte-identically, re-hash the round-trip, and update `data-release/release-provenance.json`. The same issue asks figtab to publish their media generation code and provenance accessibly to you (their release, exact revision) since your direct access to their repository is blocked — I will relay the tag here when it exists.

This issue stays open until the explorer fix is re-attached and the code access is settled.
